Level
overview
What
Level
1
builds
Level 1 builds the physical and emotional readiness that reasoning depends on. Learners form their ﬁrst
relationship with stories: they discover that stories carry feelings, that characters make choices, and that
language describes the world inside and outside themselves.
The
Thinking
Cycle
At Foundation level, the Thinking Cycle works through talk. Claim–Evidence reasoning starts at its simplest: a
spoken claim supported by a picture or a sentence from the story.
Regulation
protocol
Regulation is physical. The Butterﬂy Hug (bilateral tapping with slow breathing), movement and a natural
sensory anchor are essential, not extras.
The
four-lesson
cycle
Each story is explored in a cycle that moves learners from noticing to reﬂecting.

Lesson 9: Excavation — Discovering Feeling Fossils in The
Lantern With Two Handles
Target
Grade
Level
/
Subject
/
Duration
Grade Level: Ages 4–8 (CEFR Pre-A1 →  A1)
Subject: English Language Arts (Jurassic English™ Level 1: Foundation)
Duration: 40 minutes
Overall
Learning
Goals
Students will transition into a regulated state of physiological readiness (the "Green Zone") to actively listen to a
new story. They will excavate "Word Fossils" from the narrative: vocabulary that captures wanting to do it all
yourself, getting tired, asking for help and sharing the load.
Speciﬁc
Learning
Objectives
Students will independently or semi-independently execute the "Butterﬂy Hug" self-regulation protocol to
achieve physiological readiness.
Students will identify and extract at least one speciﬁc "Word Fossil" (e.g., ready, proud, tired, help, together,
warm) from the read-aloud text.
Students will accurately connect their identiﬁed "Word Fossil" to a corresponding visual representation (Emotion
Icon or story picture of Nuri, Bo or Grandad).
Materials
Needed
Core Text: The
Lantern
With
Two
Handles (Jurassic English original storybook; read it in the JE storybook reader
with Read to me, or from the printed student edition).
Emotion Icons: Laminated cards with clear facial expressions or physical states (ready/happy, proud, tired,
helped, together).
Word Wall Materials: Blank cards, thick markers, and designated wall space.
Fidget Fossils: Small, smooth stones for students who need a tactile anchor.
Nature Anchor: a small paper lantern, or a battery tea light that stays switched oﬀ.
Detailed
Procedure
/
Step-by-Step
Outline
Phase
1:
Regulation-Before-Reasoning
(0–5
minutes)
Activity: The Butterﬂy Hug Protocol.
Teacher Scripting Prompt: "Paleontologists, we are opening a new dig site today: an evening garden walk with a
paper lantern. Before we open the book, we must get our brains and bodies into the Green Zone. Cross your
arms over your chest, hook your thumbs, and tap left, right, left, right. Breathe quietly for 60 seconds."
Student Task: Students perform the Butterﬂy Hug, focusing on bilateral tapping and silent breathing.
Action: Distribute Fidget Fossils to ADHD-proﬁle and high-anxiety students.

·
jurassicenglish.com/products

40Licensed for one campus, one school year. © Jurassic English
Phase
2:
The
Dig
Site
—
Active
Reading
(5–15
minutes)
Activity: Read-aloud of The
Lantern
With
Two
Handles (or press Read to me in the reader).
Teacher Scripting Prompt: "Today, we are looking for Word Fossils: words that tell us how Nuri and Bo feel
inside. When you hear a feeling, place your hand over your heart."
Student Task: Active listening. Students use the gesture when they identify a target word.
Action: Read slowly. Emphasize: ready (page 1, “Ready!”), proud (page 2, “I can carry it”), tired (page 3, “Nuri’s
arm feels tired”), help (page 4, “Will you help me?”), together (page 6, “They walk together”), warm (page 6,
“One warm light”). Do not stop for grammar instruction.
Phase
3:
Excavation
—
The
Word
Fossil
Hunt
(15–30
minutes)
Activity: Identifying and claiming vocabulary.
Teacher Scripting Prompt: "Paleontologists, what Word Fossils did we ﬁnd in this story? What words tell us how
Nuri and Bo felt?"
Student Task: Students verbally share a feeling word they noticed in the text or pictures.
Teacher Move (Marking): When a student says "Tired," the teacher marks it: "You found a fossil. 'Tired' is how
Nuri’s arm felt after she carried the lantern for a long time. Let's put that on our Word Wall." Write the word
clearly on a card and place it on the board.
Action: Continue until 3–4 key feeling words are excavated and placed on the Word Wall.
Phase
4:
Linguistic
Connection
&
UDL
Expression
(30–35
minutes)
Activity: Connecting text to visual evidence (A1 Indicator prep).
Teacher Scripting Prompt: "I am holding up the picture from page 3: Nuri holding the lantern low with a tired
arm while Bo waits for a turn. Which Word Fossil from our wall matches this picture?"
Student Task: Students point to or say the matching Word Fossil (e.g., "Tired").
Diﬀerentiation
/
Accommodations
Neuroinclusive (ADHD): Provide a Fidget Fossil during the reading block. Allow standing during Phase 3 if the
student remains engaged in the hunt.
Neuroinclusive (Anxiety): Use the "Safe Start": the teacher models the ﬁrst Excavation. Never cold-call an
anxious student.
Support Tier: Pre-selected feeling cards with pictures on desks; students hold up the card when they hear the
matching word.
Core Tier: A spoken Claim plus visual evidence (e.g., pointing at the book and saying, "Nuri is tired").
Extension Tier: “Find two feelings on our wall that are OPPOSITES.” (e.g., tired and ready).
Assessment
&
Rubric
Assessment Type: Formative Observational Assessment

Reﬂection

Activity: The 2-Minute Outdoor Reset (Ecological Application).
Procedure: Lead the students outside or to a large window.
Teacher Scripting Prompt: "Nuri and Bo share one light. Look outside at the real trees. What does a tree give us:
shade, a home for birds? Does the tree need anything from us?"
Action: Allow 1–2 minutes of observation. Return, review the new Word Wall, and preview that next lesson
(Lesson 10: Strata) the class will answer "The Big Question".
Homework
/
Extension
Activities
Home Connection: "Internal Fossil Hunt." Students notice one time they feel "ready" or "warm" at home this
evening and tell a parent or guardian which Word Fossil they are feeling.

Workbook 4 · The Jurassic Thinking Cycle
1 Analyze
Page 3 · A tired hand
How do you know Nuri needs help? Find the clue on this page.
The light drops low. · She runs very fast. · She sings a song.
2 Evaluate
Page 4 · A question
Nuri asks Bo for help. Is that a good choice?
Yes · Not sure · No
3 Justify
Page 4 · A question
Tell why. Use because. You can say it, point or write.
I think it is a good choice because ___.
Word bank: tired · help · Bo · together · handle · light
4 Reflect
Page 6 · Their light
When do you ask for help? Who can you ask? Draw or tell.
